utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Good morning to everybody, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth, to the interpreters, to the legal assistants and court reporters, Madam Hollis, Mr. Waidyaratne; good morning to the Defence counsel. I see that they're all there. We continue the proceedings today, the trial of Kvocka et al. We should like to say good morning to the witness, Mr. Jasmir Okic. Have you had a good rest, Mr. Okic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But you're able to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us resume with questions put to you by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yesterday before we adjourned, you were giving evidence with regard to what happened on the 30th of May, 1992, and last you said that you were in a bus with many others.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where did the bus go, and what was the final destination?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go from where, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After you started from the SUP building, where did you proceed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the SUP building, through Prijedor, towards the post office, turning right towards the marketplace; and at the JNA street, he went right again towards the shop there; and then he went left, turned left, towards Cela and Tomasica, the road to Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, you said that in your evidence yesterday. What was the final destination of the bus? Where did the bus stop finally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear now. I can't hear very well. It's not loud enough. Could you put the volume up a bit perhaps, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could the usher increase the volume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I ask that question again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, did you finally arrive at the Omarska camp? Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation booth, are you hearing it now? Is it working? Can you hear now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's try again. Please go ahead, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you finally arrive at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What time of the day was it when you reached the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was nighttime, between 10.00 and 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After you reached the Omarska camp, were you ordered to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but I can't hear the interpretation again. It's very weak.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Can you hear me? Witness, can you hear me now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you now but sometimes the volume drops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it's due to the weather, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for example, I can't hear properly again. The volume has dropped again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it better now, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It comes and goes. It comes and goes. The Defence counsel are saying that they too cannot hear it all the time at the same volume, that it comes and goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the technical booth help us out with some suggestions to overcome this problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll try like this, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me properly now, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you say that there is a problem, that the volume comes and goes; that when there's a pause it becomes weaker, the sound becomes weaker; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the tone is low, the volume is low of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear the interpretation all right now from the booth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's try once again. If not, we're going to have a break to put things right. Mr. Prosecutor, have another go, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After you reached the Omarska camp, were you ordered to get down from the bus?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were ordered to get down from the bus, to place our hands behind our necks and to stand up against the administration building with our legs spread and our arms spread, with three fingers against the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see any other persons other than the people who came in the bus at that time?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards were standing around.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How were they dressed? Were you able to see them?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some had the SMB JNA olive-green/grey uniforms, and the others had the blue policemen's uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these people?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Then did they search you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They searched us, and then one by one we went into the entrance and they would register us and take us to the room which was referred to as Mujo's room, in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Okic, you said that you all were searched. Did you have anything on you? Did they take anything from you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just had my ID card on me, and they didn't take that away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that you were taken to a place called Mujo's room. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I spent that night there and I was transferred to the pista the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court what you mean by the place called "the pista"? Could you describe what this place is.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pista was the area between the hangar and the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How long did you stay there in the pista?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the month of June on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who were the others -- were there any others in the pista with you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. They were all civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who were they? Did you recognise any persons?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were Muslims and there was a small percentage of Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you recognise any persons?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were my relatives and neighbours. They were also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: While you were in the pista, did you see a person by the name of Ismet Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know him prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him. He lived in a settlement called Cerici, next to my own settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you call him by another name, a nickname or a petname?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His nickname was Ico.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where did you see him in the pista?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was sitting on a bench next to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What was the condition of him? Did you see him while he was in the pista?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was sitting on the bench next to the administration building and he was in a very poor condition. He was sitting there for three days. I didn't know what was happening to him. I was sitting on the pista with his brother, Saban. I asked his brother, "What has been happening to Ico?" and he said "Ico is a diabetic but he hasn't got his medicines here," they'd left them at home, and three days later he died on the pista next to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him -- did you see the body being removed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where did you see the body taken?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His body was taken off towards the "white house" and was left on the grass by the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I would give the exhibit which has been marked previously as 3/90 to the witness. I would have the assistance of the usher. 3/90 which has been marked already. May I correct my position, Your Honour. I would tender a new exhibit which the witness can use subsequently. So I would mark it 3/93. May I be corrected, Your Honour. Thank you. Could it be placed on the ELMO. THE USHER: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the photograph. Could you kindly point out the place where the body of Ismet Hodzic was placed. Just show -- point out the place where you saw the body of Ismet Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't hear the interpretation again. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The B/C/S booth, is everything going well there? I think we must have a break at this point to settle the problem. Madam Registrar, what's going on?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The engineers are already there and trying to fix the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear us now, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us try again. It would be better if the witness can hear and then we can continue. Otherwise, we're going to make a break. But let's try, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please look at the photograph which is on the ELMO. Could you point out the place where you saw the body of Ismet Hodzic placed, where it was placed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it placed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The witness points -- may it be on the record that the witness points to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Can it be marked as "O1."

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to mark it, the place where his body was, where it was laid down?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, while you were detained in the camp, were you taken for interrogation? Were you interrogated at any stage?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was interrogated in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you explain -- could you describe where you were taken for this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken for interrogation to the administration building, on the floor above, and I was interrogated in -- there's a landing in front of the office, to the left-hand side of where I was taken and interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken there by a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. His name is Zoran Miodragovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know him prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him because he worked in the same company that I worked for, Impro of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How did it happen? Did he come and call you from the place that you worked?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on the pista. And when they questioned us one by one, they would take us off one by one for interrogation from the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So this guard by the name of Zoran Miodragovic came and called you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't call us out by our names and surnames. We would just go off one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did the guard Zoran do? Did he take you to any place?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took me to the administration building, upstairs, for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a blue policeman's uniform, and he had a rifle with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him often in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, while he was working in his shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "shift"?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were three shifts and they rotated. Every 12 hours there was a different shift of guards in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you refer to this shift by any specific name, or was anybody in charge of this shift?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each shift had its leader, the leader of the shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know these leaders, all their names?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leaders of the shifts were Ckalja, Krkan, and Krle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Why did you call these people -- you referred to them by names, Ckalja, Krkan, and Krle. Did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know them before, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How did you get to know their names?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I got to know them because they would refer to each other. When talking to each other they would call each other by their surnames or by their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said "they." What do you mean by "they"? Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards. The guards, amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know which shift Zoran Miodragovic was attached to or worked in?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was in Ckalja's shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were taken for the interrogation to the first floor in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who was there?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up on the first floor there was the interrogator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How was he dressed? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he was wearing. But I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Can you remember, or do you recall what you were questioned about? Were you questioned?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked where I was during the arrest, where I worked, and why I hadn't signed the loyalty oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you explain a little more what this loyalty oath was?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that loyalty or pledge was to be signed if you wanted to continue working in the SUP, as I in fact did, in the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So did you answer these questions? What did you say when they asked you about the loyalty oath, whether you signed that oath?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that as far as the loyalty oath was concerned we were to have a meeting in the local community of Prijedor 3, in the SUP of Prijedor, as a joint police force, but in the meantime the Hambarine village was shelled and the meeting never came about. And so that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he question you about the weapons that you had?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he asked me about weapons, whether I had returned my weapons and my uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During this interrogation, other than the person who questioned you, were there any other persons present?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the guard present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After the interrogation, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the interrogation I was returned to the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Okic, during the time that you spent in the pista, did you spend any time in the restaurant during the nights?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent a number of nights in the restaurant building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: While you -- the time you spent in the restaurant building in the night, did you witness an incident of shooting?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of Nasic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Mehmedalija Nasic. He was a man from a place called Cejreci who worked in the cellulose factory of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see an incident involving him?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were ordered to sit down on the floor and we did sit down, but Nasic got up and started talking. He said, "People, why are we here? We ought to be going home to our own houses and to live with our neighbours." And he moved forward slightly, and when he moved forward, the guard from the outside shot and hit him and he fell down in the restaurant, on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said -- did you see the guard who shot at that instance?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the guard called Pavlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see the guard at that instance, and where was he?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where was he?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the outside, towards the "white house," on that side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That is, outside the restaurant building.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know Pavlic before the war?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How did you get to know the name of Pavlic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt it because the guards would call each other out by surnames or by nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you describe Pavlic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was about between 170 and 180 centimetres tall; he had dark hair and he had some grey hair here in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to Nasic thereafter, after the shooting?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nasic fell, and then two people took him out through the window and he was left on the grass, the area I mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see any other persons injured during this shooting?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three other persons were injured who were behind Nasic's back, under the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know the names of these people?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two brothers, Delkic, and I don't know the name of the third person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know what happened to them after the shooting?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there and then I would see them again in the camp, but I had no contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After the time that you spent on the pista, were you transferred to any other place?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the pista I was transferred to Room 26, on the upstairs floor in the hangar. This was in the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How were you transferred there? How did you get to the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because all of us from the pista would go to sleep in the restaurant. Some people went to number 26, some to number 13. Because I had to go upstairs every night and come out in the morning, and they would beat us on the way there and on the way back, so I moved to Room 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You again said "they." Whom are these people that you referred to as "they"?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards. The guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What was the condition in the room that you called Room 26?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conditions were intolerable. This was a room roughly 25 by 25 metres, and there were 300 to 400 men inside. The roof was made of aluminum. The temperature was 30 outside so inside it was even warmer. There were only two small windows on the sides which were half open. So if we had to go to the toilet, a guard would come and ask, "Who wants to go to the toilet?" and "Form groups of five." We would form a group of five. The first group would go and come back all bloody; we saw that they had been beaten, and then we would just lie down on the floor and not go to the toilet at all. Then the guard would just shut the door and say, "Don't anyone ask to go to the toilet again." So we had to relieve ourselves in the room we slept in. Some 50 per cent of us in that room relieved themselves there. Some people had bags, some boots, and these bags stood there all night and it was only in the morning that they could be cleaned away. Then there were lice. Everyone had lice. Whenever there were hairs on our body, they were full of lice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you given an opportunity to wash yourself, or were you provided with that kind of hygienic facility?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only once did I have an opportunity to wash myself in Omarska. With a hydrant hose we were washed once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you describe, explain, how that happened?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bathing, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day they came and said that we should go downstairs, that we would be washed, and it was on the grass there, outside the hangar. They told us to take our clothes off. They took a fire hydrant, with a hose and very high pressure, and they really did it for fun, not to wash us. They just hosed us all over with the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Again you said "they." Who are you --

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards. The guards. I mean the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During the detention that you -- during your detention in Room 26, were you provided with water and food?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would get one jerrycan of water for all of us, and we were all terribly thirsty and hardly anyone had enough to drink, because we would snatch the water away from each other. We went to eat once a day, and this was in great haste. And sometimes we would ask others whether there were guards beating and if they were beating then we wouldn't go and eat at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you describe what you got to eat while you were detained?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a piece of bread and a cooked dish which was really almost entirely water.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Okic, while you were detained in Room 26, did you see a person by the name of Mehmed Alisic inside the room?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mehmed Alisic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a private carrier from Prijedor, living in Tukovi. He had his own private company for transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you see any incident involving him taking place while you were in that room?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in July, in Room 26. Mehmed was in the bedroom and he was walking around in the room, but before that the guard said, "Don't let me see anyone standing or walking around." And Mehmed was walking and the guard opened the door and the guard shot, opened fire, and Mehmed fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see Mehmed being taken out?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two of us were told to carry him out, and he was carried out, and then two or three more shots were heard, and I don't know anything more. I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You heard the shots being fired for the second time after he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you know the person that -- you said that there was a guard who shot. Did you know this guard by name?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Pirvan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you describe how he looked.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was about 180 centimetres tall. He had light coloured hair and it was balding; he had hair only at the back of his head. And he was wearing an olive-grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know -- did you see this guard named Pirvan often in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would see him when his shift was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recall which shift that was?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Further, during your detention in that room, number 26 -- that you referred to as number 26, did you see a person by the name of Gordan Kardum?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Gordan Kardum was brought to our room. I don't know from where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you refer to him by another name, a short name?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gogi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know him before the war?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him. He worked at the petrol station in Prijedor held by Energopetrol. I knew him as a worker of Energopetrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When you saw him in that room, in room number 26, did you notice anything? How was he? What was his condition?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a sweatsuit, and when he came back his trousers were rolled up and his feet were black. Three days later he couldn't even go for lunch. He was lying down. Later on he got a bit better and he went for lunch, and one day when we went to eat, he was lying there dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that he couldn't walk. Did you know why he couldn't walk?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't walk from his injuries. He had been beaten and he was all broken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During your detention, were you beaten separately or individually?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would regularly be beaten on the way to eat and coming back. That was a regular occurrence. You would get one, two, or three blows. But only once when I was really badly beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When was that? Can you describe that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the second half of July or mid-July, I think. On the fiftieth [sic] Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coming back from lunch to Room 26, we were running through the corridor and a guard was standing at the door to an office. As I ran past, he called out, "You, big-headed one." I turned around and the neighbour in front of me turned around too, and he pointed at me and said, "You come here." He told me to go into the office. He moved away from the door. As I went in, he hit me with a cable that he had in his hand and he hit me on the back. Then he faced me and told me to give him 100 German marks. I said, "I have no money on me. I didn't bring it and I don't have any." Then he said that I should cross over to the other room across the corridor. I went there and he came and said to me, "I'm coming back in five or ten minutes. Get 100 marks for me." I said, "You can kill me but I don't have the money." He came back and I said, "I have no money." There were two benches linked together next to the wall. He told me to lie down on those two benches. I did and I held onto the benches with my hands, and he hit me with this cable on the back. After some time, when he stopped beating me, he ordered me, this guard ordered me to go to the bedroom and to prepare there 100 German marks. I went there. I knew that no one had any money. I said that the guard was asking for these 100 marks. No one had any money and no one gave me any. When the guard came to fetch me, I went out into the corridor and said that I didn't have the money, that no one had it to give to me. Then again he said, "You have five to ten minutes to collect watches, chains, and rings, and I'll come back." I went back to the bedroom again and I told the others what he had told me, the people who were lying in Room 26. I collected a few watches, and when he came, I went to the corridor and showed them to him. He chose one watch and took it, and then he told me I was free, that I could go back to the bedroom, the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: This guard, did you know him? Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him often in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In his shift he would always sit to the left of the "white house." There was a chair there and he would sit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know to which shift he belonged?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When did you leave the camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Omarska on a Thursday. The 6th of August, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where were you before you were transferred from Omarska? In which part of the camp were you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last few days, I was in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did anybody come and call you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First a list of names was read out by the driver of the bus who drove Ckalja's shift. I don't know his name. He read out the list and he said, "The people whose names I read out should go to the pista and the others remain in the dormitory." My name was called out; I went to the pista. When we were all there on the pista, Zeljko Meakic came and read out a list and he said, "If I don't call out someone, he should tell me." Two men were not called out and he asked, "Did I not call out anyone?" and two men said that he hadn't been called out and he separated the two from our group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you referred to a person by the name of Zeljko Meakic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard in the camp that he was the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what kind of uniform he wore.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him often in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I went for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How were you transported -- taken to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken there by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the period from the 6th of August until the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When you left Trnopolje -- how were you released from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A condition for my release from Trnopolje was for me to bring a certificate that I was leaving all my property to Republika Srpska, and on the basis of that certificate I was released. My wife got the certificate in Prijedor and brought it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After you left Trnopolje on the 14th of August, 1992, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That was to Raskovac?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Raskovac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When did you leave -- did you leave Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Bosnia on the 12th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During the time that you were released from Trnopolje and the time that you left Bosnia, you were at home.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you able to go out?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went out to the yard but no where else, no where further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was afraid because the Serbs were all in uniform, they were all armed, and your life was at risk all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, could you describe to the Court whether there were any long-term effects that you face due to the detention in the camp, due to the abuse that you underwent during your detention in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in May 1992, I weighed 105 kilos. When I reached Trnopolje, there was a weighing machine, and I weighed 78 kilos. My mental condition, when I left Bosnia to a third country, I would wake up at night screaming, saying, "They have come to pick me up again." And to this day I have problems. When I go to sleep, I keep seeing this film all over again in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What is the property that you had back home in Bosnia that you had to leave?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to leave everything. I had 7.000 square metres of land, a house built in 1991, a car, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender a photograph to the witness and ask a few questions with regard to a exhibit which I have marked, 3/91.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please look at the photograph. Now, you referred to a person -- could you identify -- do you know those people in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Would you place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you identify the people in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left, this is Mirsad Alisic, son of Latif, and this is Gogi on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The person whom you referred to as Gogi is the person whom you earlier testified as Gordan Kardum.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Bear with me, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In your testimony, with regard to the time that you spent in Room 26 and when I questioned you about the water, how it was supplied, you said that you were provided a jerrycan. Could you describe what was the size of this can which was provided to you and how it was provided?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the can contained between 10 and 15 litres of water.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You testified that there were 300 to 400 prisoners in that room.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I also ask you a question with regard to Gordan Kardum. You said that you saw his body.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Where did you first see it?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Room 26, in the middle of the room. He was lying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And thereafter where did you see the body?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was carried out and I didn't see him again. I don't know where he was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Also you said that during your interrogation you were questioned about the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did they ask you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me whether I had returned my weapons. I said -- I told him what I had as weapons, who I spoke to in SUP, that they came to the local community and that I had surrendered my weapons, my ammunition and uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you tell him as to whom you returned it?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You also said that you were questioned about the loyalty oath.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you explain what he asked you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told him that I had been a member of the reserve police force and that I had weapons which I had surrendered, and then he asked me why I hadn't signed this loyalty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: To whom? Loyalty to whom?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Serb police, the Serb station in Prijedor, the Prijedor Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have your permission to have the witness have Exhibit 77 -- 3/77D, it be given to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, please see that diagram. Are you familiar with that? Do you understand what it is?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the upper floor of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you place it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Is this the place where you were detained while in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In July.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you show where Room 26 is?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, B1. B1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I conclude my direct examination, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne. Witness, you are now going to answer questions which the Defence attorneys are going to ask you according to the order which Mr. Krstan Simic is going to announce. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the basis of our consultations, I will have a few brief questions for this witness and the rest of the Defence team have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Mr. Krstan Simic. You have the floor. Your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Okic.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In your testimony you said you were a member of the reserve police force or militia, whichever.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: For us to get a clear insight into your status, was it your military duty or assignment, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who deployed you into the police or militia?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1980 -- in the 1980s, when Tito died, I was mobilised and became part of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In the case of any emergency situations, extraordinary situations, you would also --

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We joined Raskovac and Prijedor 3 at Berek.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yes, but you were always a member of the police force, were you not?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. And you had uniforms, weapons.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The same day, I was issued this the same day in 1980, when Tito died.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So your rifle and ammunition, did you take that home?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took it home.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was it at your house the whole time?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When a selection was carried out for members of the reserve police force on the basis of this military assignment or duty, did these individuals have to have a high moral character and criteria, along those lines?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So were the members of the reserve police force, was this an important post in view of the current system, and a post of respect?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You always used the word "guard" during your testimony. In view of the fact that you were a member of the reserve police force, did the individuals who appeared within the guard system, were they members of the reserve police force, in fact?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Omarska? I don't know who -- which composition they belonged to because some were wearing police uniforms and some were wearing the SMB olive-green/grey uniforms. So I don't know what formations they actually belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When you had these contacts with the members of the security detail, did you happen to notice that individuals wearing the SMB uniforms, the uniforms of the former JNA, had police insignia which they just put on their uniforms, identifying them as being members of the police force? Did you happen to notice that?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: As a reserve policeman, you said that you saw to security matters. You mentioned the bridge?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the bridge over the River Sana next to the Prijedor Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. So the police provides security, does it not?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should now like to have the witness shown document -- a document marked D17/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, Mr. Simic, I would like to say that there was an inaudible response to a question that you asked the witness. Perhaps you should make greater pauses between questions and answers. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Okic, you have a document before you. Would you read the title, the heading, and who adopted this -- compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the left-hand side, in the left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it out? "The Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Ministry of the Interior, the Centre of the Security Services in Banja Luka, the Public Security Station of Prijedor, the 31st of January, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: The Public Security Station of Prijedor, was that the police station in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, could we have the document placed on the ELMO, please, so that we can all follow. Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you would probably need the English version. Mr. Okic has just received the B/C/S version. So the document you need is D17/1A.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to read point 6 carefully. It's at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it out? "The security services at the collection centre shall be provided by the Omarska Police Station with an adequate number of policemen who shall be present at the collection centre at all times and shall organise guard duty seconding to the on duty-on call-off duty principle."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Okic, as a member of the reserve police force with a lot of experience, does this clearly define the assignment of the members of the Omarska police station?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was their task?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was in a concentration camp and here it says "Collection Centre." Those are two different notions, two different concepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Okic, I'm asking you what the task of the Omarska Police Station was. You can consider what you like; the Court will rule. What was the task?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To organise the work of the security service and the guard duty, according to the duty-on call-off duty principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago you spoke about an individual who died for health reasons while at Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you see in the interval that any member of the medical service arrived, like a doctor or a nurse?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear or see that the gentleman asked for help, medical assistance, of anybody because of his problems?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When you spoke about the time that you spent on the pista, you said you spent some 20 days.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June?

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yes, in June. Did you spend a whole night on the pista, or would you be transferred at night, every night?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent one or two nights on the pista, and the rest of the time I would either go to the hangar or Room 26 or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago the unfortunate incident where Mr. Mehmedalija Nasic was killed. Could you say in relation to the location, the spot, that is to say, where the restaurant was, where were you standing? Where were you actually standing at the time? Try and describe that to us, please.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was about three to four metres away from me, in front of me, towards the food distribution line. So he was between me and the food distribution line, looking down the restaurant. So I was looking at him diagonally from the position where the shot came.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: That is to say, how could you see the place from which the shot came?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is difficult to explain. If I could have a photograph, perhaps it would be easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: 3/77A. Now you have the diagram of the restaurant in front of you. Could you indicate to us where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yes. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: And Mr. Nasic, where was he?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: And Mr. Pavlic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the outside here.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you like a policeman. Was the movement made by Mr. Nasic unexpected? You said that he suddenly moved forward after saying what he said.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Well, was it unexpected, an unexpected movement?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just started to move forward. He was there and then he took two or three steps forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In which direction?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He moved towards this line here. As this man was there, he moved diagonally this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you hear any warnings issued beforehand?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So there was just his movement, precipitous movement, and then the shot; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Mr. Waidyaratne, any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Okic, you were questioned by Mr. Simic with regard to the incident with regard to Nasic. Mr. Nasic was inside the restaurant, was he?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And this guard, where was he?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was outside, the other side of the glass or wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How many detainees were inside the restaurant roughly?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you exactly, but the restaurant was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And all these other people were seated.

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Nasic armed or did he have any weapons with him at that time?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How old was Mr. Nasic? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was between 55 -- about 55, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne. Madam Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You mentioned that among the detainees, the shifts were often identified by the name of the shift commander or his nickname, such as you mentioned Krkan, Ckalja, and Krle. Would you have recognised any of those shift commanders by sight while you were at Omarska? I mean, would you have known who they were if they walked by?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would. I think I would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My next question, then, is: In any of the incidents that you mentioned, which included some beatings and two shootings, I think, and an extorsion, attempt to get money, were any of those shift commanders either present or within visible range of the occurrence, the shooting, the beating? Did you ever see any of them around the premises when any of those incidents occurred?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. Mr. Okic, I have two questions myself. The guard that we spoke about earlier on who was on the exterior of the restaurant building, was he alone or was he accompanied?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him alone. I didn't see anybody else with him at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My other question. You spoke about Room 26 and you identified Room 26 on a diagram as being "B1." Why do you call the room "Room 26"?

utterances.speaker: JASMIR OKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. That's how we all called it; we all called it Room 26. When I got there, everybody called it Room 26. I don't know why, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. You have concluded your testimony. Mr. Waidyaratne, we have an exhibit, 3/73; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I tender Exhibit 3/93 to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And the Defence? Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no objection, and I speak on behalf of all the Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The exhibit is admitted into evidence accordingly. Mr. Okic, thank you very much for coming here. Before you leave, I just want to ask you if there is anything which you would like to say which has not yet been asked of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I can say is that I don't want anybody to have to go through what we went through in Omarska, us prisoners, and those in charge of Omarska should be adequately punished so that it be a lesson to others and not to have the same thing repeated again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I hope that everybody can hear your wishes. Thank you very much for coming here, and we wish you bon voyage back to your place of residence. The usher will now accompany you out of the courtroom. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it is -- as it is almost 11.00, this would be a good time for a break before continuing with the next witness. As it is six minutes to eleven, let us have a half-hour break now, and we shall resume afterwards. Madam Hollis, I don't know whether you wish to say anything before we break.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: We are now going to have the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: at 2.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of June, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
